# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #28): Power-Stage Model, DShot Timing, and Reference Netlist

## 0. Scope, Assumptions, and Architecture

I don't have a locked BOM for Job #28, so every number below comes from a **declared reference design**. Each equation is parametric. Replace the bracketed values with your selected parts' datasheet values (at the matching Tj, not 25 °C) and the results scale directly.

**System partition.** In this kind of stack, the 48 kHz PWM is generated by each ESC's own MCU (AM32 or BLHeli_32 class), not by the H743. The H743 running ArduPilot only:
- emits bi-directional DShot600, and
- decodes the eRPM telemetry that comes back.

The model is split along that boundary.

| Parameter | Symbol | Reference value |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | V_bus | 6S, 25.2 V max (22.2 V nominal) |
| Burst phase current (per ESC) | I_pk | 80 A, DC-equivalent in conducting legs |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz, complementary (synchronous rectification) |
| MOSFET | Q | 60 V, R_ds(on),25 = 1.2 mΩ max, Q_g = 50 nC, Q_gd = 10 nC, Q_gs2 = 4 nC, V_plateau = 3.5 V, R_g,int = 1 Ω, Q_rr = 60 nC, Q_oss = 60 nC, V_SD = 0.8 V, R_θJC = 1.5 K/W |
| Gate drive | V_drv | 10 V; R_src = 2.5 Ω, R_sink = 1.5 Ω (driver), R_g,ext = 3 Ω |
| Dead time | t_d | 50 ns per edge |
| Shunt (per ESC) | R_sh | 0.5 mΩ |
| Commutation | | 6-step trapezoidal (AM32 default) |
| Board | | 30.5×30.5 mm class, 6-layer, 2 oz outer and 2 oz inner power planes, 24 MOSFETs (1 per switch position) |

> **Engineering flag up front.** A nano-class 4-in-1 ESC carrying 80 A on all four channels simultaneously is **burst-limited by thermal capacitance, not steady-state rated**. The math in §3 shows the realistic burst window is on the order of 1–2 seconds. "80 A burst" must be specified with a duration and duty cycle, or it is not a meaningful rating.

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Temperature-dependent R_ds(on)

$$R_{ds}(T_j) = R_{ds,25}\,[1 + \alpha (T_j - 25)],\qquad \alpha \approx 0.0055\ \text{K}^{-1}$$

At T_j = 125 °C: R_ds = 1.2 × 1.55 = **1.86 mΩ**.

### 1.2 Current path in 6-step with synchronous rectification

At every instant, exactly two phase legs conduct:
- **PWM-on:** HS(A) → motor → LS(B). Two FETs in series.
- **PWM-off:** LS(A) (sync rectifier) → motor → LS(B). Two FETs in series.

The PWM duty cycle therefore cancels out of conduction loss (dead time excepted, see §2.4):

$$P_{cond,ch} = I^2 \cdot 2R_{ds}(T_j) + I^2 R_{sh} + I^2 R_{Cu}$$

Plugging in the reference values:

| Term | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| FETs | 80² × 2 × 1.86 mΩ | **23.8 W** |
| Shunt | 80² × 0.5 mΩ | **3.2 W** |
| Copper (est. 0.3 mΩ path) | 80² × 0.3 mΩ | **1.9 W** |

### 1.3 Per-FET distribution

Each FET carries current for about 1/3 of the electrical period. At high eRPM the loss averages to roughly 23.8/6 ≈ **4 W per FET**.

At **low eRPM or stall (launch, prop strike)**, averaging fails. One FET pair can sit in a single commutation state for milliseconds, so each FET sees **~11.9 W**. That is the worst case for die-temperature spikes.

### 1.4 RMS form (for sinusoidal/FOC firmware variants)

$$I_{rms,FET} = \frac{I_{pk}}{2}, \qquad P_{cond,ch} = 6 \cdot \left(\tfrac{I_{pk}}{2}\right)^2 R_{ds} = 1.5\,I_{pk}^2 R_{ds}$$

Under FOC, define I_pk as the sinusoidal phase peak. At 80 A peak this gives 17.9 W.

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only the PWM leg hard-switches. The low-side partner of the conducting pair is static, and the sync rectifier turns on after its body diode conducts, so it soft-switches.

### 2.1 Gate current through the Miller plateau

$$I_{g,on} = \frac{V_{drv} - V_{pl}}{R_{src} + R_{g,ext} + R_{g,int}} = \frac{10 - 3.5}{6.5} = 1.0\ \text{A}$$

$$I_{g,off} = \frac{V_{pl}}{R_{sink} + R_{g,ext} + R_{g,int}} = \frac{3.5}{5.5} = 0.64\ \text{A}$$

$$t_r = \frac{Q_{gs2}+Q_{gd}}{I_{g,on}} = 14\ \text{ns}, \qquad t_f = \frac{14\ \text{nC}}{0
